newsitem.title: USA: US stock index futures end mixed, S&Ps slightly off.
newsitem.headline: US stock index futures end mixed, S&Ps slightly off.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures closed mixed, with rallies in the U.S. bond market and U.S. dollar pulling most contracts to daily highs late in the day, traders and analysts said.
"We really just jumped on the bandwagon," one stock index futures floor source said. "But I don't see any reason why these contracts should back down from here."

December Standard & Poor 500s turned briefly higher, rising to 759.50, as futures prices for Midcap 400s and Nasdaq 100s extended their opening gains. Strong gains in technology stocks such as IBM supported Nasdaq all day, they said.
However, the bond and dollar rallies gave new life to the S&P 500 futures market, which was beset by tax-related selling and year-end profit-taking at the start of the day.
"Aside from the opening and the late afternoon, trade was very lackadaisical down here," one futures trader said.

Arbitrage buy programs were reportedly touched off in the afternoon when December traded at a 3.00 to 3.10 point premium to the cash index. Arbitrage sell programs were at a 0.70 point premium to cash S&Ps, and fair value was at 1.50 points.
Nikkei futures remained sharply lower on continued spread trading, traders said. December Nikkeis, which expire on Thursday, December 12, closed down 390.0 at 20,715.

At the end of pit trade, December S&Ps were off 0.25 at 758.00, KBT Value Lines were up 3.80 at 686.80, New Composites were up 0.20 at 399.25, Midcap 400s were up 2.05 at 258.45 and Nasdaq 100s were up 10.25 at 847.75. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com))
